title: Clashing Tides In The Tasman Sea
gist: Gavekal's Rohan Daswani notes the Australian and New Zealand dollars, historically correlated via China commodity demand, have recently diverged: AUD is supported by coal/LNG demand and a hawkish RBA-style central bank, while NZD suffers from weak growth, high unemployment, a property slump and emigration to Australia. (Paywalled teaser only.)

insights.claim: The Australian and New Zealand dollars have historically moved broadly in tandem against the US dollar because both economies are exposed to global, especially Chinese, commodity demand.
insights.speaker: Rohan Daswani
insights.so_what: Baseline: the AUD-NZD correlation is a commodity-beta relationship; breaks in it are tradeable relative-value signals.

insights.claim: Australia's exports are dominated by metals and energy while New Zealand specializes in agricultural products such as dairy and meat, giving the two currencies different commodity sensitivities.
insights.speaker: Rohan Daswani
insights.so_what: AUD/NZD effectively expresses an energy/metals vs. dairy/meat terms-of-trade spread.

insights.claim: The Australian and New Zealand dollars have recently moved in opposite directions because of diverging monetary policy expectations and economic prospects, breaking their traditional relationship.
insights.speaker: Rohan Daswani
insights.so_what: Favors long AUD/NZD while the policy divergence persists.

insights.claim: Strong demand for Australian coal and liquefied natural gas exports, plus a more hawkish central bank, has been supporting the Australian dollar.
insights.speaker: Rohan Daswani
insights.so_what: Watch coal/LNG prices and Australian rate expectations as AUD drivers.

insights.claim: The New Zealand dollar has been weighed down by weak domestic growth, high unemployment, households hurt by a prolonged post-Covid property slump, and emigration of New Zealanders to Australia for jobs and health care.
insights.speaker: Rohan Daswani
insights.so_what: Structural NZ weakness (housing, labour outflow) suggests NZD underperformance may persist beyond a cyclical blip.
